notes: For k_j = 2*4^j+5 every l in L with k_j*l in L has >= 2j-1 base-4 digits, so m(k_j) > k_j^2/128 (j >= 3): no exponent C < 2 works. Exact m(k) for odd k < 2e7: m(k) < k^2/48 for 37 <= k < 2e7, extremal family k_j with m = (4^(2j+1)-7*4^j+48)/48 (3 <= j <= 12). Lean: chk_complete, least_133 (m(133)=333), least_517 (m(517)=5425). Outside Lean: the all-j lower bound (reduction of the carry chain of 5l + 2*4^j*l to a finite lockstep automaton, certificate/family_lower.py) and the data for k < 2e7 (certificate/minm2.c).

sources.cite: J. H. Loxton, A. J. van der Poorten, An awful problem about integers in base four, Acta Arith. 49 (1987) 193-203

prior_art.note: No bound on the least multiplier found in print; Guy's k = 133 is the j = 3 member of the extremal family.
